FOLLOW-UP, MEASURED -- the stale column-count sentence in anomaly.rs. Upgrading an inference I posted earlier into a checked fact, because a followup whose remedy is a guess is the least reliable part of the record.

The trailing sentence of the comment block on
`evaluable_columns_measured_surface_on_the_292_column_census` reads:

    The test's NAME carries the census's metric-column count
    (290 CSV columns less `seed`, `pin_set` and `refusal`)

Measured against the committed census on main, not reasoned about:

    $ git show origin/main:book/src/laboratory/generated/the-census/rows.csv \
        | head -1 | awk -F',' '{print NF}'
    295
    295 - 3 = 292
    $ test name -> on_the_292_column_census

So the sentence should say 295, not 290. 290 - 3 = 287, which matches nothing.
It rotted when THE MURRAIN moved the surface 290 -> 295; that campaign updated
its own new paragraph (which correctly says 295) and left the older trailing
sentence beneath it untouched.

I AM DELIBERATELY NOT FIXING IT, and the reason is worth stating. The queued
pinfix c15f86bddd66 ADDS lines to that same comment block. A competing edit to
the same block from a tooling branch risks a conflict that bounces a vetted
candidate over a comment. The fix is one line and costs nothing to fold into
whatever next legitimately edits that block.

Nothing mechanical will ever catch this: every count in it is prose, the test
name is right, and the assertions are right. It is only wrong to a reader.
